page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Reduce the angles
steps.margin_note: First mark. Reduce so that every angle becomes 20° or 40°. The sin 200° picks up a minus, and that minus is what turns the sum into a difference.

recall.must_convey: That the angles reduce to cos20°, −sin20° and sin40°.
accept: cos three forty is cos twenty, sin two hundred is minus sin twenty, sin one forty is sin forty
reduce so everything is in twenty and forty degrees
the sine of two hundred picks up a minus sign
angles ni twenty and forty ga marchali, sin two hundred minus vasthundi

steps.why: Reducing to 20° and 40° is deliberate: those two angles differ by 20° and sum to 60°, and 60° is a value we know exactly.
common_mistakes: Reducing to angles that do not match each other.

steps.label: Apply cos(A+B)
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The minus makes the expression cos20°cos40° − sin20°sin40°, which is exactly cos(20° + 40°) = cos60°.
lines: = cos(20° + 40°)   [∵ cosA cosB − sinA sinB = cos(A+B)]

recall.must_convey: That the expression becomes cos20°cos40° − sin20°sin40° = cos(20°+40°) = cos60° = 1/2.
accept: the minus makes it cos A cos B minus sin A sin B which is cos of A plus B equal to cos sixty
apply the compound angle formula to get cos sixty which is a half
it becomes cos of twenty plus forty which is cos sixty
cos A plus B formula tho cos sixty vasthundi, half
the answer is cos sixty equals a half

steps.why: The formula needs a MINUS between the two products. The minus from sin 200° supplies it — without that reduction the formula would not apply.
common_mistakes: Using cos(A−B), which needs a plus between the products.
